title: Prove a gate against the committed tree, never the working tree: reconstruct the files it asserts on from the merge commit and run it there

title: Every new gate ships a clean-checkout proof

evidence.note: PR #172 fixed the replay in governance/dispatch/claims.py

title: A frontier is a point-in-time property: never recompute a historical decision from today's snapshot

summary: The claim gate reported closed issue #139 as the eligible frontier from a board snapshot that was 19 minutes old; the reader consumed stale data as truth because it had no freshness rule

action: Add a snapshot-staleness check to the claim gate and store claims conflict-free, so an answer derived from a stale snapshot is refused rather than returned

title: A snapshot's timestamp is part of its meaning

summary: The AgentConsole go-live was designed against agent-orchestrator's own GCP Cloud Run pipeline (epic #607) and published to the operator as 'one deploy away', while the fleet's live-hosting contract (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, owner directive 2026-09-04) fixes the remote shared-services cluster as the only live host and had deliberately removed the Cloud Run config; the deployment contract was documented in the peer modules the whole time

action: Scavenge and declare the AgentConsole hosting contract from the peer modules (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md + contrib/shared-services, shared-services infra) and hand the run half to its owners as a direction issue

evidence.note: AgentConsole lane A: the shared-services hosting handoff + a bootable image

remediation: Before choosing a host for any go-live, read the peer modules' deployment contracts and the owner directives they encode (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; shared-services infra) and scavenge the project ids, service accounts, secret names and edge config from them; a documented hosting contract is an input, never an external boundary.
title: A deployment contract documented in a peer module is an input, not an unknown boundary

summary: Epic #607's go-live was declared for months and never exercised: the declarations asserted nothing was live, and the console image recipe had never been built (its only builder was the retired Cloud Run route), so a defect inside the artifact - portal/Dockerfile installed PyYAML but not cryptography, exiting 1 at boot - was invisible until the go-live ran.

action: Add a binding, self-proving gate for the AgentConsole hosting contract (scripts/check-agentconsole-hosting.sh, registered in scripts/verify.sh) that asserts the image recipe, the overlay, the together-promoted surfaces, the live-host declaration and the fail-closed env contract offline, and mutates one property per rule on every run

title: declared is not exercised: a declared artifact (an image recipe, an overlay, a contract doc) is unfalsifiable until a control reads or runs it - give every declaration a gate that can fail, or it drifts from the tree silently
